name: Sikagard-63 N
paste:
SIKAGARD®-63 N: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sikagard®-63 N, August 2025, Version 04.01 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/9/sikagard_-63_n.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sikagard®-63 N where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (August 2025, Version 04.01).
1.2 Product description. Sikagard®-63 N is a 2-part,novolac epoxy resin based, chemical resistant, protective coating. It can be used on many types of structures or elements for cementitious, metallic and epoxy resin binder substrates. The chemical resistant properties provides surface protection from aggressive chemicals that can cause rapid degradation.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. Sikagard®-63 N may only be used by experienced professionals.
1.4 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer - Chemical resistant protective coating on.
    - Concrete
    - Stone
    - Cementitious mortars
    - Renderings
    - Epoxy cement
    - Epoxy resin-based products
    - Steel
1.5 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer - Chemical resistant protective lining for.
    - Silos
    - Bund linings
    - Chemical mixing tanks
    - Chemical containment tanks
    - Fuel and oil tanks
    - Sludge tanks
    - Industrial chemical areas
1.6 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer - Anti-corrosion coating on steel elements within.
    - Food processing plants
    - Sewage treatment works
    - Chemical and pharmaceutical facilities
    - Beverage facilities
1.7 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.8.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sikagard®-63 N
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: NOVOLAC EPOXY CHEMICAL RESISTANT PROTECTIVE COATING
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Sustainability.
    - Conformity with LEED v4 MRc 4 (Option 2): Building Product Disclosure and Optimization - Material Ingredients
    - Conformity with LEED v2009 IEQc 4.2: Low-Emitting Materials - Paints and Coatings
2.3 Certificates and test reports.
    - Potable Water approved to AS/NZS 4020:2018 - Testing of products for use in contact with drinking water
    - CE Marking and Declaration of Performance to EN 1504-2 - Surface protection product for concrete - Coating
2.4 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - AS/NZS 4020:2018: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Certificates And Test Reports (p.1).
    - EN 1504-2: cited with a stated property or value; listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Certificates And Test Reports (p.1); Product Information > Product declaration (p.2).
    - EN ISO 2811-1: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Density (p.2).
    - ISO 4624: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile adhesion strength (p.2).
    - EN 24624: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile adhesion strength (p.2).
    - EN ISO 7783-1: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Diffusion resistance to water vapour (p.2).
    - EN 12944-4: referred to in instructions or limitations. Where: Application Instructions > SUBSTRATE PREPARATION (p.3).
    - EN 14879: referred to in instructions or limitations. Where: Application Instructions > SUBSTRATE PREPARATION (p.3).
2.5 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Good chemical resistance
    - Good temperature resistance
    - Low VOC emissions
    - High build
    - Impervious to liquids
    - Easy to mix
    - Applied by brush, roller or airless spray
2.6 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Epoxy resin
    - Appearance and colour: Standard colour: ~RAL 7032 (pebble grey); Other colours on request.
    - Density: Resin mixed:~ 1.44 kg/l; Value at +23 °C (EN ISO 2811-1)
    - Product declaration: EN 1504-2 - Surface protection product for concrete - Coating
2.7 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Solid content by mass: ~100 %
    - Solid content by volume: ~100 %
    - Tensile adhesion strength: > 1.5 N/mm² to concrete; > 15 N/mm² to steel; > 10 N/mm² to aluminium (ISO 4624) (EN 24624) (EN 24624)
    - Chemical resistance: Resistant to many chemicals. Contact Sika Technical Services for additional information.
    - Resistance to UV exposure: Loss of gloss, yellowing and chalking will occur with UV exposure. This will not compromise performance.
    - Diffusion resistance to water vapour: µH2O ~100 000 (EN ISO 7783-1)
2.8 Temperature resistance.
    | Exposure | Dry heat |
    | Permanent | +40 °C |
    | Maximum 3 days | +60 °C |
2.9 Systems. Standard Three Coat System: (DFT: from 600um - 800um) Primer: Sikafloor 160 or 161 + 1st Coat: Sikagard®-63 N + 2nd Coat : Sikagard®-63 N . Fibreglass Laminate System: (DFT: from 1000um - 1200um) Subject to Glass thickness Primer : Sikafloor 160, Fibreglass, Sikafloor 160 + 1st Coat: Sikagard®-63 N + 2nd Coat : Sikagard®-63 N . Sikagard EpoCem 720 System: (DFT: 1200um +) Subject to thickness of SikaGard EpoCem 720: Typically used on High Wear, Damaged or High moisture content substrate applications: SikaGard EpoCem 720 + 1st Coat: Sikagard®-63 N + 2nd Coat : Sikagard®- 63 N . Please refer to individual Product Data Sheets and consult the Sika Technical Department for specific Consumption Priming and Coverage Information pertaining to project requirements: Please see Important Considerations section at the bottom of this PDS
2.10 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Shelf life: 12 months from date of production
    - Storage conditions: The product must be stored in original, unopened and undamaged packaging in dry conditions at temperatures between +5 °C and +30 °C. Always refer to packaging.
2.11 Packaging.
    | Part A | 8.70 kg container |
    | Part B | 1.3 kg container |
    | Refer to current price list for packaging variations |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (August 2025, Version 04.01) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality. Substrates must be clean, dry and free of all contaminants such as dirt, oil, grease, coatings, laitance, surface treatments, loose friable materials and and any other surface contaminants that could affect adhesion.
3.3 Substrate preparation.
    - Concrete / Stone / Cementitious mortars & rendering Concrete must be at least 3–6 weeks old.
    - Substrates must be prepared mechanically using suitable abrasive blast cleaning or planing / scarifying equipment to remove cement laitance and achieve an open textured gripping surface profile suitable for the product thickness.
    - High spots can be removed by grinding.
    - Weak substrates must be removed and surface defects such as blow holes and voids must be fully exposed. Repairs to the substrate, filling of cracks, blowholes/voids and surface levelling must be carried out using products from the Sikafloor®, Sikadur®, Sikagard® and Sika Monotop® range of materials. Products must be cured before applying Sikagard®-63 N.
    - Steel / aluminium
    - Surfaces must be prepared mechanically using suitable abrasive blast cleaning, grinding, rotating wire brush or other suitable equipment to achieve a bright metal finish. Reference must be made to the preparation levels in the following standards if compliance is required:
    - ISO EN 12944-4: level Sa 2 ½
    - NACE International Standard: SSPC-SP 10 “near white metal blast cleaned”
    - EN 14879, part 1
    - Apply a suitable compatible primer on the prepared steel as soon as possible to prevent oxide development. Contact Sika Technical Services for additional Epoxy resin-based products
    - Surfaces must be prepared by abrading using suitable equipment.
    - General
    - On high absorbent, non-cementitious based substrates a suitable primer must be used. Contact Sika Technical Services for additional information.
    - All dust, loose and friable material must be completely removed from all surfaces before application of the product and associated system products, preferably by vacuum extraction equipment.
    - Avoid dew point conditions before and during product application.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (August 2025, Version 04.01) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Mixing ratio: Part A : Part B = 87 : 13 by weight
    - Consumption: ~0.25-0.4 kg/m² per layer
    - Layer thickness: ~175-300 microns per layer.
4.3 Pot Life.
    | Temperature | Time |
    | +10 °C | ~30 minutes |
    | +20 °C | ~20 minutes |
    | +30 °C | ~10 minutes |
4.4 Waiting time to overcoating.
    | Temperature | Min. | Max. | Full Cure |
    | +10 °C | ~9 hours | ~3 days | ~14 days |
    | +20 °C | ~5 hours | ~2 days | ~9 days |
    | +30 °C | ~4 hours | ~1 day | ~5 days |
4.5 Mixing. Prior to mixing all parts, mix part A (resin) using an electric single paddle mixer (300–400 rpm) or other similar equipment to mix liquid and all the coloured pigment until a uniform colour has been achieved. Add part B (hardener) to part A and mix part A + B continuously for 3.0 minutes until a uniformly coloured mix has been achieved. To ensure thorough mixing, pour materials into a clean container and mix again for at least 1.0 minute to achieve a smooth consistent mix. Excessive mixing must be avoided to minimise air entrainment. During the final mixing stage, scrape down the sides and bottom of the mixing container with a straight edge trowel or spatula at least once to ensure complete mixing. Mix full units only. Mixing time for A+B = ~4.0 minutes
4.6 Application.
    - Reference must be made to further documentation where applicable, such as relevant method statement, application manual and installation or working instructions.
    - Prior to application, confirm substrate moisture content, relative air humidity, dew point, substrate, air and product temperatures.
    - Apply Sikagard®-63 N onto the prepared substrate evenly using a roller, brush or airless spray at the required consumption rate.
4.7 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all tools and application equipment with Sika Thinner C immediately after use. Hardened material can only be removed mechanically.
4.8 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Do not apply Sikagard®-63 N on moist substrates.
    - Sag resistance on vertical surface is < 300 μm.
    - Do not use to produce glass fibre reinforced linings.
    - Protect freshly applied product from rain, condensation and water for at least 24 hours.
    - For consistent colour matching, ensure the Sikagard®-63 N in each area is applied from the same control batch numbers.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. +10 °C min. / +30 °C max.
5.3 Relative air humidity. ≤ 80 %
5.4 Dew point. Beware of condensation. The substrate and uncured applied floor material must be at least +3 °C above dew point to reduce the risk of condensation or blooming on the finish.
5.5 Substrate temperature. +10 °C min. / +40 °C max
5.6 Substrate moisture content. Substrate moisture content Maximum 4% when measures using Sika® - Tramex meter ( at the time of application). Please note that the moisture content must be < 4 % pbw when using the CM measurement or Oven-dry-method. No rising moisture according to ASTM (Polyethylene-sheet).
5.7 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.8):
    - Protect freshly applied product from rain, condensation and water for at least 24 hours.
5.8 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Density: Resin mixed:~ 1.44 kg/l; Value at +23 °C (EN ISO 2811-1)
    - Tensile adhesion strength: > 1.5 N/mm² to concrete; > 15 N/mm² to steel; > 10 N/mm² to aluminium (ISO 4624) (EN 24624) (EN 24624)
    - Diffusion resistance to water vapour: µH2O ~100 000 (EN ISO 7783-1)
5.9 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.10 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sikagard®-63 N, August 2025, Version 04.01, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/9/sikagard_-63_n.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sikagard®-63 N Part B, version 23/02/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/u/sds-sikagard-63npartb.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS SikagardÂ®-63 N Part A, https://aus.sika.com/dam/dms/au01/q/sds-sikagard-63nparta.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Ecology, health and safety - Directive 2004/42/ce limitation of emissions of.
    - VOC
    - According to the EU-Directive 2004/42, the maximum allowed content of VOC (Product category IIA / j type sb) is 500 g/l (Limits 2010) for the ready to use product. The maximum content of Sikagard®-63 N is <500 g/l VOC for the ready to use product.
6.4 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.5 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.6 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
